radiology_report:
Antoni van Leeuwenhoek
Department of Radiology
Date: 15 November 2024
Exam: mpMRI Prostate
Clinical indication: PSA 6.9 ng/mL, suspected prostate cancer

FINDINGS:
The prostate measures 40.33 mL in volume. T2-weighted imaging demonstrates a focal hypointense lesion in the right peripheral zone, measuring approximately 12 mm in maximum dimension. This lesion exhibits restricted diffusion on DWI (high b-value signal) with corresponding low ADC values. Dynamic contrast-enhanced imaging shows early, marked enhancement of the same region. No extracapsular extension or seminal vesicle invasion is identified. No suspicious lymphadenopathy is seen.

IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS 5 lesion in the right peripheral zone. Prostate volume 40.33 mL. PSA density 0.171 ng/mL/mL. Clinical T stage cT2. csPCa predicted probability 0.8314881.

previous_notes.author: Dr. E. Mulder (GP)
previous_notes.text: Patient presented with rising PSA levels. Previous PSA was 2.7 ng/mL in October 2023, now 4.3 ng/mL. DRE was performed and a nodule was palpated. Referred to urology for further evaluation and possible biopsy.

pathology_report:
Biopsy 1 (May 2024):
Histological examination of the prostate biopsy cores reveals atypical cells in loose, partly also abortive tubules with polymorphic hyperchromatic nuclei and sometimes nucleoli. The Gleason score is 3+4, corresponding to ISUP grade group 2. No cribriform or intraductal patterns identified. The tumour is located in the peripheral zone, right.

Biopsy 2 (January 2025):
Histological examination of the prostate biopsy cores reveals atypical cells in loose, partly also abortive tubules with polymorphic hyperchromatic nuclei and sometimes nucleoli. The Gleason score is 3+4, corresponding to ISUP grade group 2. No cribriform or intraductal patterns identified. The tumour is located in the peripheral zone, right.

Summary:
The histological findings across the two biopsy timepoints remain stable with ISUP grade group 2 disease.
